pattern: proxy finish LIGHT (proxy_finish.py stage_light + proxy_finish_light.py): the frozen Pixal3D sheet proxy kept as generated (geometry + texture), made watertight, decimated, baked, optionally reposed with bones

refloor.why: sheet_proxy already floored the FEET (both feet reach z 0.000: -x foot x -1.25..-0.2, +x foot x 0.25..1.45; no tail / hem below them): the window only confirms the foot contact (z0 = 0) and rescales x(6.65 / 6.583) = 1.010 to the sheet front height

dense.why: the big angular head: facets, both horns + crown spikes, eyes, nose dot, mouth (proxy slabs z 4.5..6.58, x -1.1..1.1, y -1.1..1.2, x1.010 to the stage frame); vg_weight 0.3 so the eye boxes below sit denser

the +x eye socket (proxy socket surface centre 0.622,-0.299,5.563, long axis 0.6 u along (0.65,0.76,0), half-height 0.15): held denser so the glow / pale interior and the blue rim land on separate faces
the -x eye socket (proxy socket surface centre -0.326,-0.604,5.483, long axis 0.66 u along x, half-height 0.15): held denser so the glow / pale interior and the blue rim land on separate faces

light.ao_why: AO baked on the watertight low itself: the proxy's crystal shards (neck / shoulder growths, leg spikes) are thin overlapping shells that black-hole AO rays (crystal_canine / vulture / frost_calf lesson); ray length 0.45 u so only real crevices (armpits, crotch, under the head) darken: the sheet's ice is pale and evenly lit
light.bake_drop_interior_why: proxy faces with solid on both sides (crystal shards sunk into the body) left out of the bake source so the cage stays tight

recolour3d.name: pale_ice
recolour3d.why: UNIT NOTE: the proxy reads dark teal on the panel; that is mostly the panel light (proxy texture median 133,177,222, not teal), but the texture IS darker and its pale facets cyan-cast: proxy pale texels (b* > -15, 23 % of samples) median 181,217,226 (L* 84.4) vs the sheet's pale ice (front-view mask, eroded 4 px; 37 % of pixels) 213,231,239 (L* 90.6; chip 233,233,232). Pale texels to 222,236,244 (~4 % above the sheet so basecolor = albedo x AO lands on it), the proxy's facet shading kept at half contrast. v1 run 1 at gamma 0.5 / soft 5 posterised the ice into flat white and blue blotches (head close-up): gamma 0.85 + a 10-unit b* blend band keep the proxy's own gradients

recolour3d.name: blue_ice
recolour3d.why: the blue facets: proxy blue texels (b* <= -15) median 120,165,221 (L* 66.8) vs the sheet's blue ice (front view) 145,189,241 (L* 75.4; chips 177,210,243 / 105,163,236). To 150,194,244 (~3 % above for AO), the proxy's facet light/dark pattern kept (gamma 0.6) so the crystal still reads faceted. gamma 0.85 + soft 10 (run 1 at 0.6 / 5 read posterised)

recolour3d.name: eye_rim
recolour3d.why: coordinator gate v1: the painted eyes read as cloudy white blotches; the sheet draws a clean almond eye with a crisp darker-blue outline (front / side view eye-outline pixels L* < 55: median 45,87,173 / 51,87,156 / 49,92,164). The whole socket opening + 0.01 u is painted the outline blue first, then the iris below covers all but a 0.035 u band. socket-opening outline traced per eye on a z-buffered render of the proxy looking straight into the socket (+x eye: view dir (0.766,-0.643,0.1) through 0.622,-0.299,5.563; -x eye: (-0.29,-0.95,0.1) through -0.326,-0.604,5.483), smoothed (Chaikin x3); the outline is tiled by spheres that never reach past it (greedy radii 0.06..0.007 u, each sphere's 2D footprint inside the outline), centred on the proxy surface

recolour3d.name: eye_iris
recolour3d.why: the pale glowing iris (sheet front-view eye interior median 194,233,243, core 213,240,247): the socket opening eroded by the 0.035 u rim, painted uniformly (the proxy's own light gradient kept at gamma 0.3 for a soft centre), no colour select so there is no blotchy edge; socket-opening outline traced per eye on a z-buffered render of the proxy looking straight into the socket (+x eye: view dir (0.766,-0.643,0.1) through 0.622,-0.299,5.563; -x eye: (-0.29,-0.95,0.1) through -0.326,-0.604,5.483), smoothed (Chaikin x3); the outline is tiled by spheres that never reach past it (greedy radii 0.06..0.007 u, each sphere's 2D footprint inside the outline), centred on the proxy surface

glow3d.name: eyes
glow3d.why: the glow confined to the iris: low faces whose centroid lies in the iris outline eroded by a further 0.01 u (tiled spheres, radius +0.01 so centroids just off the proxy surface still count) -> eye_glow (sheet eye colour x 0.7); the rim stays unlit. Coordinator gate v1: the run-3 glow (3 spheres r 0.12 per eye + a colour select) spilled as blotches

yaw.why: v2 (artist 2026-10-17: 'our characters should be symmetrical ... spring pig and the child frost giant seem to have issues with this'): Pixal3D built the WHOLE child turned about Z (the sheet's slightly turned front): the best mirror plane of every height slab of the v1 low sits 22..26 deg off X = 0 (feet 22, shins 24, hips 22, belly 26, chest 26, neck 20, head 22, hands 26), so the 'yawed head', 'swung arms' (+x back y +0.75..1.2, -x forward -0.4..-0.8) and 'staggered legs' (0.7 u in y) are one root turn. Whole-low yaw sweep (-30..-16 deg, about a point on the body plane): mirror p99 1.062 -> 0.262 at -23.5 (-22..-25 within 0.01); about = to = (0, 0.2) puts the body plane on x 0 (best x shift -0.08 at -23.5). One rigid turn (no vertex moves relative to another); the repose below then works in this turned frame

chains.name: arm
chains.why: v2, turned frame (surface-sample slab centroids of the arm outer part |x| > 1.05): points = the +x arm, points_R = the -x arm as generated: shoulder inside the shoulder growths (z 3.9: +x y 0.12 / -x 0.0), elbow (z 3.0: 1.39, 0.24 / -1.39, 0.10), wrist (z 2.2: 1.67, 0.30 / -1.59, 0.13), crystal tip (z 1.55 / 1.5: 1.72, 0.30 / -1.63, 0.15): after the root turn the +x arm still hangs 0.10..0.17 u further back and 0.05..0.09 u further out; the repose makes the pair mirror-symmetric (mean)

chains.name: leg
chains.why: v2, turned frame (slab centroids, legs split at x 0): points = the +x leg, points_R = the -x leg as generated: hip (z 2.6, x 0.42 / -0.46), knee (z 1.4: 0.53, 0.02 / -0.61, 0.01), ankle (0.81, -0.01, 0.55 / -0.83, 0.0, 0.45), toe (foot front, y -0.55; +x 0.18 / -x 0.08): the +x foot is LIFTED (its lowest vertex z 0.099, the -x foot -0.009): the repose makes the pair mirror-symmetric (mean) and plants both feet

rig.spine_why: v2, in the light.yaw-turned frame (body plane x 0): spine on the midline (torso slab centroids x -0.09..+0.02 at z 1.6..4.2); hips (0, 0, 2.9), spine (0, 0.05, 3.45), chest (0, 0.1, 4.0), neck root (0, 0.05, 4.4), head pivot (0, -0.05, 4.75; neck top, the chin reaches down to z 4.6 in front); the head bone runs from the pivot 0.9 u horizontally along the FACE direction to z 5.6: perpendicular to the iris-centre line (the eye line yaw is -4.14 deg after the root turn: (-0.065, -0.947)), so the repose heading turns the face straight ahead

clips.why: PLACEHOLDER (movement + height are the open artist questions): idle = breathe + the kit's arm sway; walk = a chunky child step

config._doc: LIGHT finish of the raw Pixal3D proxy (seed 56, sha 0edeb461) + v2 symmetric rest pose (light.yaw root turn + repose). Points: refloor / dense / recolour3d / glow3d boxes in the stage-1 frame (refloored at the feet, x1.010 to the sheet front height 6.65); rig / repose / focus in the light.yaw-turned frame; sheet units.

targets.why: artist 2026-10-17: symmetric rest pose. After the root turn the legs are close (joint mirror error 0.04 / 0.08 / 0.10 / 0.10 u hip..toe) but the +x foot hangs 0.099 u above the floor: both legs carried onto their mean (one mirror-symmetric pair), both feet planted on z 0; falloff 0.03 keeps the leg moves off the pelvis (offline on the v1 low: leg edge stretch max 1.20, none > 1.25)
the arms mirror-symmetric at the mean (joint error 0.12 / 0.14 / 0.19 / 0.18 u after the root turn: the +x arm hung further back / out); no plant, the crystal tips hang free

targets.heading: -y
targets.why: the face straight ahead: after the root turn the iris-centre line is still yawed -4.14 deg (the face turned a little less than the body: +x eye 0.07 u ahead); the head bone points along the face, so heading -y turns it +4.14 deg, spread neck 2.07 / head 4.14; the head is RIGID (below)

rigid.why: the whole head (horns, crown spikes, both v1.1 almond eyes, chin down to z 4.6) moves as ONE rigid body with the head bone: never deformed or re-sculpted; the eye paint rides on the UVs; the ramp (z 4.3..4.55) blends into the neck

repose.why: v2 (artist 2026-10-17, 'our characters should be symmetrical head turns are done through posing so our models remain flexible'): the proxy's turn is undone as ONE rigid root turn (light.yaw) plus BONES (proxy_finish_repose) in the turned frame, never by mirror-averaging geometry; the extra crown spikes are design detail and stay

high.rule: marching tets of the whole remesh grid (no mirror)

low.method: collapse decimation: uniform to 300000, then 18000 with the dense boxes calibrated

dense.rule: dense boxes weighted 0.02 (vs 1) in the collapse decimation; the factor bisected until the boxes hold density x the rest's triangles per area

bake.source: the proxy mesh itself (not the remesh)

rows.why: the glow confined to the iris: low faces whose centroid lies in the iris outline eroded by a further 0.01 u (tiled spheres, radius +0.01 so centroids just off the proxy surface still count) -> eye_glow (sheet eye colour x 0.7); the rim stays unlit. Coordinator gate v1: the run-3 glow (3 spheres r 0.12 per eye + a colour select) spilled as blotches

glow3d.rule: faces -> glow palette regions (emission -> Glow -> Emission Color); rgb white keeps the baked albedo

mirror_after.rule: every vertex mirrored in X about the plane -> distance to the nearest surface (0 = exactly symmetric)

yaw.why: v2 (artist 2026-10-17: 'our characters should be symmetrical ... spring pig and the child frost giant seem to have issues with this'): Pixal3D built the WHOLE child turned about Z (the sheet's slightly turned front): the best mirror plane of every height slab of the v1 low sits 22..26 deg off X = 0 (feet 22, shins 24, hips 22, belly 26, chest 26, neck 20, head 22, hands 26), so the 'yawed head', 'swung arms' (+x back y +0.75..1.2, -x forward -0.4..-0.8) and 'staggered legs' (0.7 u in y) are one root turn. One rigid turn (no vertex moves relative to another); the repose below then works in this turned frame
yaw.rule: p' = Rz(deg) (p - about) + to on every vertex of the finished low (one rigid turn about Z, the root orientation; no vertex moves relative to another)

mirror_before.rule: every vertex mirrored in X about the plane -> distance to the nearest surface (0 = exactly symmetric)

stretch_all.rule: edge length after / before the repose, edges with a moved vertex

repose.rule: LBS with the contract rig's weights (+ rigid pins), yaw-only straightening (+ lift), applied as rest

stretch_leg.rule: edge length after / before the repose, edges with a moved vertex

stretch_arm.rule: edge length after / before the repose, edges with a moved vertex

stretch_neck_head.rule: edge length after / before the repose, edges with a moved vertex

self_intersections.rule: intersecting triangle pairs sharing no vertex (BVH overlap)

mirror_before.rule: every vertex mirrored in X about the plane -> distance to the nearest surface (0 = exactly symmetric)

mirror_after.rule: every vertex mirrored in X about the plane -> distance to the nearest surface (0 = exactly symmetric)

floor.rule: stage 1 floored the FEET at z 0; the centring puts the lowest point at 0

facing.rule: shell centroid -> the front-most midline point of the shell (proxy finish default)

mirror.rule: every vertex mirrored in X about the plane -> distance to the nearest surface (0 = exactly symmetric)
